description: We're the Felix Dolor, here to dominate the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
summary: CEI-SAT is a browser city-planning game that turns real data into decisions. You are Calgary's Planning Director, commanding a planning satellite above the city, with one 10-minute term to make Calgary more equitable. The map is built from the City of Calgary's 2024 Equity Index: 288 census tracts grouped into 24 real districts, each rated on six measures such as health, economic opportunity and climate. On top of that, the game layers NASA Earth observations: a cloud-free NASA HLS Landsat image of the city, MODIS greenness (NDVI) and MODIS summer land surface temperature, averaged for every district. Players see which neighbourhoods are hottest and least green from space, and that data changes the outcome: a park cools a hotter-than-average district more, so satellite data steers where you build. Every building has trade-offs, residents voice real local needs, and disasters strike mid-term. At the end, the game compares your Calgary with the real index. The goal is to show how Earth observation and local equity data together can guide fairer city planning, in a form anyone can play on a phone or laptop.
details:
What it does

CEI-SAT is a city-planning game you play in the browser. You are Calgary's Planning Director, in command of a planning satellite above the city, with one 10-minute term to make Calgary more equitable. Play it here: https://felix-dolor.github.io/NASA-City-Planner/

The city is built from real data. Calgary's 288 census tracts are grouped into 24 districts named after real communities, and each is rated on six measures from the City of Calgary's 2024 Equity Index: Economic Opportunity, Accessibility & Amenities, Population Health, Belonging & Safety, Human & Social Wellbeing, and Climate & Environment.

How it uses NASA data

  • NASA HLS Landsat (L30) true-colour image of Calgary from August 2025, chosen as a cloud-free summer scene. It sits under the game map and can be toggled with the NASA view button or the N key. The game zooms from orbit down to the city through this image.
  • MODIS Terra 16-day NDVI (greenness) and MODIS Terra 8-day daytime land surface temperature, averaged over summer 2025 for every census tract and then every district. These appear as two Plan layers and on each district card next to the Calgary average.
  • The data changes gameplay: a park built in a district that NASA measured as hotter than Calgary's summer average cools it more and adds extra Climate and Health benefit. Players are steered toward the hottest, least green neighbourhoods, such as Forest Lawn and Marlborough.

All NASA imagery comes from NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services). A script in the repo (tools/build_nasa.py) downloads the layers, decodes the colour scales back into NDVI and temperature values, and samples them inside every census tract. We cross-checked the results against the City's own tree canopy and heat columns: greener tracts have more canopy, and greener areas run cooler.

How you play

Residents in each district offer missions based on their district's real numbers. You zoom into a district and place buildings on real-feeling lots: parks, clinics, libraries, transit, factories, data centres and more. Every building has trade-offs, such as pollution reaching nearby homes or transit raising rents, and a live preview shows every rating that changes before you build. Disasters such as floods and a roaming tornado strike mid-term. At the end, a report compares your Calgary with the real 2024 index.

Why it matters

Equity data and Earth observation are usually read separately and by specialists. CEI-SAT puts them together in a form anyone can play on a phone or laptop, and shows that where you build matters: the same park does more good in a hot, under-served district. The game's effect model is a simplified game mechanic, not a prediction of what real investments would do.

Tools

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no frameworks or build step, drawn on an HTML canvas. Python for the data pipeline. Hosted on GitHub Pages. The interface works with mouse, touch and keyboard.

Use of AI

Parts of the code, the data scripts and this text were written with help from an AI coding assistant (Claude Code). The trailer was captured from the game by an AI-written script and carries a visible "Code and trailer made with help from AI (Claude Code)" watermark. Its music is an original track synthesized by AI-written code, with no samples; this is also noted in the video file's metadata.
